statements.text: The Biden-Harris Administration is also addressing the significant risks that AI presents to our safety and security, democracy, economy, and civil and human rights.

statements.text: The Administration is tackling these risks head-on by securing voluntary commitments from major AI companies, issuing a landmark Executive Order on Artificial Intelligence, and releasing for public comment a draft Office of Management and Budget (OMB) policy for the use of AI by the U.S. government.

statements.text: Global investment and competition in AI are increasing, and our continued leadership – whether public sector or private – is not assured.

statements.text: For example, China has moved to replicate the model and investments of the DOE’s National Laboratory system and is investing heavily in its own AI capabilities and workforce.

statements.text: Retaining leadership in AI will require developing trustworthy AI systems that can be deployed for high-consequence uses, from healthcare to aerospace.
